one_liner: Senior Executive running ATF's three forensic labs, fire research lab, quality office, and forensic auditing unit from Beltsville, Maryland.
fit_summary: This is a Senior Executive Service job that requires proven executive leadership of multi-site accredited forensic laboratories, forensic research, and investigative support programs. Daniel's emergency-management consulting experience at IEM and policy knowledge do not match the Mandatory Technical Qualifications, which are effectively pass/fail. Daniel should not invest heavily here and should target entry and mid-level roles instead.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens or nationals), but the job is SES and veterans' preference does not apply.
You must show all five ECQs and all three MTQs within a resume of two pages or less. Resumes over two pages are ineligible, and separate narratives are not accepted.
MTQ1 requires leading multi-site forensic lab systems or large technical enterprises under accreditation frameworks such as ISO/IEC 17025.
You need a Top Secret security investigation, a drug screening, and an OGE 278 financial disclosure.
You must show progressively responsible senior executive-level leadership experience by the closing date of November 4, 2026.
keywords: allocation of human and material resources
strategy: Be honest with yourself: without executive leadership of forensic labs or law-enforcement technical programs, the rating panel will likely screen you out at the MTQs.

Spend your effort instead on GS-7 to GS-11 public-facing roles, such as FEMA, DHS, DOJ program analyst, and public affairs jobs, or on Virginia and Prince William County emergency management positions.
If you apply anyway, use one concise two-page resume that maps your IEM work to each ECQ and MTQ, citing scope, budget, staff, and results only where they are true.
Use ECQ1 language (rule of law, American system of government) to showcase your policy knowledge, since it is your strongest match.
Use this posting as a long-term model of the SES competencies you will need to build over a federal career.
resume_bullets: [Title], IEM, [dates], [hours/week]: Supported [government client] on [disaster recovery/preparedness program] by coordinating [number] stakeholders across [agencies/jurisdictions].
Managed [budget/resources of $X] for [project], applying [process or technology improvement] to achieve [verifiable result].
Served as liaison between [client agency] and [partners such as local officials or the public], producing [reports/briefings] delivered [on time/at a frequency].
interview_questions: Describe how you led a multi-site laboratory or technical enterprise through ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation.
How have you validated new forensic methods or integrated AI or data analytics into a law-enforcement environment?
Tell us about cutting costs or reallocating resources while maintaining quality standards.
How have you held staff accountable while leading an organization through change?
watch_outs: The MTQs require specialized forensic and law-enforcement executive experience that Daniel's background does not show.
The job is on-site in Beltsville, MD with no telework, which means a long commute from Manassas.
The position requires a Top Secret investigation, OGE 278 financial disclosure, and a possible one-year probationary period.
A resume over two pages, or separate ECQ narratives, will be rejected automatically.
